tiling.name: Patterns: Dress the Architecture
tiling.truth: A source, a copying rule and a receiving surface each contribute to a pattern. Keep one fixed and change another: what returns as the same, and what becomes possible for a body?
tiling.description: Return to the familiar disco with independent pattern and palette controls, then let the foundry machines supply live pattern and colour to architectural walls and floors. Continue through motif operations, symmetry, volume, appearance, shaders and dressed bodies.
learning_objectives: Reuse addressed pattern values with a replaceable palette and independent clocks
Read a small palette-index source through wrapped addresses; distinguish source copies, held images and saved recipes
Separate a reflected read from reversing entries within each stored row
Explain face axes, cell width and full motif width; distinguish physical metres from normalized UV counts
Test reflection and glide across their repeating unit without claiming a full wallpaper-group proof
Use a layer index in a palette lookup while separating stored data from slice visibility
Compare fixed values across carriers and viewing conditions without prescribing perception
Write a tiny repeat-and-offset texture sample in a supplied studio host; state exactly what its saved recipe can transfer
tiling.deferred_reason: No maps are currently deferred from this nine-hall sequence. The earlier separation of colour and pattern work is recorded in curation_history.
tiling.notes: Current route: familiar disco with independent palette control; shared sources and receivers in the foundry; fixed-motif comparisons; an addressed corridor; bounded symmetry comparisons; volume; appearance; and a shader recipe carried onto garments and the runway. The nine maps are cumulative encounters, not a complete derivation of the wallpaper-group classification. The historical sequence key remains tiling; patterngeneration is a separate sequence.
content: Pattern_Disco: Arrangement, palette and independent clocks
Pattern_Foundry: Shared sources, held receivers and patterned architecture
Tutorial_Pattern: Keep the motif; change the relation between copies
Array_Patterns: Follow an address across floor and walls
Symmetry_Seventeen: Compare rules and delimit the classification
Pattern_Temple: The temple wears the rule - one desk dresses floor, walls, columns and dome
Ribbon_Patterns_01: A source acquires a third addressed direction
Ribbon_Patterns_02: Stored values meet carriers and shading
Ribbon_Patterns_03: A saved shader recipe travels onto bodies
tiling.museum_recovery_note: The original colour/pattern separation and perimeter-wall recovery remain part of the layout history. Current membership is the nine-map list above; inspect each live map for its authored configuration.
tiling.ribbon_consolidation: 2026-09-09: seven former colour ribbon rooms consolidated into three annexes; authored colour/tiling copies take precedence. Remaining exhibits occur once across the annexes.

artifact_groups.rationale: Palle, 2026-11-02: 'these should be added to the pattern sequence, but we can also use the vertical plane when we curate the space'. The 46 mosaic floor artifacts (commons/artifacts/pompeii_mosaic_floor) belong to Patterns: a floor is a rule laid out, the same argument as the tile and the wallpaper group. They are not yet a hall: walkable as a framed field in the playground recipe Mosaic_Pompeii_Floors (Void trial mosaic_decks, floor 3 of playground_floors), and on the vertical plane as wall boards with artifact_tilt -90 (example mosaic_wall). pompeii_meander_floor draws nothing yet (its script has helpers but no build).

curation_history.recorded_context: Original 7–9 September curation notes, preserved on 19 September 2026; these describe an earlier four-room state and are not current capability claims.
curation_history.deferred_reason: THE UNBRAIDING, 2026-09-07 (Palle). colour was carrying two threads: a COLOUR thread (Nails, Pillar, Walls, Context_Placed) and a PATTERN thread (Pattern_Foundry, Symmetry_Seventeen), diagnosed by the red-thread pass on 2026-09-03 — 'three of the seven rooms contain no colour argument at all'. The pattern rooms leave for a sequence of their own, joined by Tutorial_Pattern and Array_Patterns from array_tutorial. Evidence they are one sequence: pattern_tile_mirror stands in three of the four (Symmetry_Seventeen joins on vr_tile_editor alone), pattern_tile_4x4 in two, pattern_maker_station in two, vr_tile_editor in two. colour's stated truth — 'context, not wavelength' — now applies to every room in colour.
curation_history.notes: Born 2026-09-07 out of colour and array_tutorial. It partly undoes the 2026-08-24 fold that dissolved symmetry into colour's census room — stated as a reversal, not smuggled. NOT named for shaders: there are zero .gdshader files under commons/shaders and two shader-named tokens in the registry, and a sequence should not be named for work that does not exist yet. RENAMED 2026-09-07 from `pattern` to `tiling` at Palle's instruction, to keep it distinct from patterngeneration — 'Shaders & Patterns: The Book of Shaders', 25 maps, which stays OUT of the spine for now. Every artifact in these four rooms is a tile, loom, mill or wallpaper piece, and the sequence ends on the seventeen wallpaper groups, which is the classification of plane tilings. `tiling` names what is built; `patterngeneration` names what is designed.
curation_history.museum_recovery_note: 2026-09-09: retain current pattern configurations inside perimeter walls. These four maps are owned by tiling, never colour.

tiling.learning_objectives_status: Nine complete tutorials and reduced learner bindings are present. Current loom and garment encounters remain optional. 12 October continuity pass reuses Colour helpers and verifies the printed studies; physical learner review remains open.

local_review_history.decision: Separate sources and storage scopes; preserve reflective comparisons; close with a bounded UV sampling lesson in the existing studio.
